newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia monopoly committee starts UES case.
newsitem.headline: Russia monopoly committee starts UES case.

text.p: Russia's state anti-monopoly committee has begun a case against Unified Energy System over allegations it interfered with Irkutskenergo power exports to Mongolia, a committee official said on Friday.

Andrei Tsyganov, head of the restrictive business practices department, told Reuters the case had been brought in connection with allegations UES restricted the independence of Irkutskenergo in the export of electricity worth $4.5 million.
UES runs the national grid in Russia and generates power of its own. Irkutskenergo, based in Siberia, is one of only two regional generating companies in which UES does not have an equity stake.
"We have started from the position that...UES has a dominant position not only on the market for power generation but also for transmission," Tsyganov said.
He said that under committee rules, cases had to be examined within a month but that this could be extended.
According to research by stockbrokers MC Securities, Irkutskenergo last year reached a supply agreement with the Mongolian authorities.
However, Russian media reports said the electricity supplies needed to use the national grid and that UES effectively stopped the exports.
No comment was immediately available from either company.
